concepts.name: Genes and alleles
concepts.summary: Recall that a gene is a unit of heredity at a locus and that alleles are alternative versions of it.

concepts.name: Genotype versus phenotype
concepts.summary: Explain that genotype is the allele combination an individual carries while phenotype is the resulting observable trait.

concepts.name: Dominant and recessive alleles
concepts.summary: Explain how a dominant allele masks a recessive one in heterozygotes.

concepts.name: Homozygous and heterozygous
concepts.summary: Recall the terms for carrying two identical or two different alleles at a locus.

concepts.name: Chromosomes and diploid inheritance
concepts.summary: Understand that each parent gives one chromosome of each pair so offspring carry two alleles per gene.

concepts.name: Gametes and allele segregation
concepts.summary: Understand that the two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation so each gamete carries one.

concepts.name: Mendel's pea experiments
concepts.summary: Recall how Mendel crossed pea lines and observed the 3:1 ratio in the F2 generation.

misconceptions.text: Dominant alleles are always more common or stronger than recessive alleles.
Offspring inherit all their traits from only one parent, or a blend of the parents' traits.
Genotype and phenotype mean the same thing.

concepts.name: Punnett square monohybrid crosses
concepts.summary: Construct Punnett squares to predict genotype and phenotype ratios for one-gene crosses.

concepts.name: Test cross
concepts.summary: Use a cross with a homozygous recessive individual to determine an unknown genotype.

concepts.name: Probability rules in genetics
concepts.summary: Apply multiplication and addition rules to calculate probabilities of genetic outcomes.

concepts.name: Dihybrid crosses and independent assortment
concepts.summary: Predict two-gene outcomes, including the 9:3:3:1 ratio, assuming genes assort independently.

concepts.name: Incomplete dominance and codominance
concepts.summary: Distinguish patterns where heterozygotes show an intermediate or both phenotypes.

concepts.name: Sex determination and sex-linked traits
concepts.summary: Predict inheritance of X-linked traits in males and females.

concepts.name: Multiple alleles and blood groups
concepts.summary: Work out ABO blood group inheritance using three alleles with dominance and codominance.

misconceptions.text: A Punnett square result means exactly that ratio will appear in every family or small sample.
If parents have had three children of one phenotype, the next child is more likely to be different.
Incomplete dominance shows that alleles blend permanently and cannot separate in later generations.

concepts.name: Pedigree analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse pedigrees to infer the mode of inheritance and the likely genotypes of individuals.

concepts.name: Gene linkage and recombination
concepts.summary: Explain how linked genes deviate from independent assortment and how crossing over produces recombinants.

concepts.name: Genetic mapping from recombination frequency
concepts.summary: Calculate recombination frequencies from cross data to order genes and estimate map distances.

concepts.name: Chi-square test for ratios
concepts.summary: Use a chi-square test to judge whether observed offspring counts fit expected ratios.

concepts.name: Epistasis and gene interaction
concepts.summary: Interpret modified dihybrid ratios such as 9:3:4 or 12:3:1 as interactions between genes.

concepts.name: Penetrance and expressivity
concepts.summary: Distinguish incomplete penetrance from variable expressivity when genotype does not predict phenotype cleanly.

concepts.name: Chromosomal mutations and nondisjunction
concepts.summary: Analyse how nondisjunction, deletions, duplications, inversions and translocations alter inheritance.

concepts.name: Point mutation types and effects
concepts.summary: Classify substitutions and indels and predict their effect on the protein.

misconceptions.text: Linked genes can never be separated and always are inherited together.
A non-significant chi-square result proves the hypothesized ratio is correct.
Epistasis is the same as dominance between alleles of one gene.

concepts.name: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
concepts.summary: Derive and apply expected genotype frequencies and the assumptions required for equilibrium.

concepts.name: Evolutionary forces on allele frequencies
concepts.summary: Analyse how selection, genetic drift, gene flow and mutation shift allele frequencies.

concepts.name: Inbreeding and heterozygosity loss
concepts.summary: Explain how non-random mating changes genotype frequencies and exposes recessive disease.

concepts.name: Quantitative traits and heritability
concepts.summary: Evaluate what heritability estimates do and do not say about genetic influence on a trait.

concepts.name: Epigenetic and imprinting effects
concepts.summary: Analyse inheritance patterns that depend on parent of origin or chromatin state rather than DNA sequence.

concepts.name: Mitochondrial inheritance
concepts.summary: Interpret pedigrees showing maternal transmission and heteroplasmy.

concepts.name: Genetic risk calculation with Bayes
concepts.summary: Evaluate carrier or disease risk by combining prior pedigree probability with conditional evidence.

misconceptions.text: Dominant alleles increase in frequency over generations simply because they are dominant.
High heritability means a trait is fixed by genes and cannot be changed by environment.
Hardy-Weinberg proportions describe real populations that are evolving.

concepts.name: Linkage disequilibrium and haplotypes
concepts.summary: Assess how nonrandom allele association arises and how it supports mapping and inference.

concepts.name: Genome-wide association study design
concepts.summary: Evaluate the design, confounding by population structure, multiple testing and interpretation of association studies.

concepts.name: Coalescent and population structure inference
concepts.summary: Judge inferences about ancestry, divergence and demographic history from genetic variation.

concepts.name: Detecting natural selection signatures
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence for selection against drift using sequence and frequency patterns.

concepts.name: Complex trait genetic architecture
concepts.summary: Critique models of polygenic architecture, gene-environment interaction and the limits of polygenic prediction.

concepts.name: Designing genetic studies
concepts.summary: Design a cross, family study or sampling strategy with suitable power and controls to answer a genetic question.

concepts.name: Ethics of genetic information
concepts.summary: Evaluate the ethical and interpretive issues of genetic testing, screening and data use.

misconceptions.text: A significant GWAS hit identifies the causal variant.
Polygenic scores predict individuals equally well across all ancestries.
Any allele-frequency pattern showing a shift implies natural selection.
